title: DNC Auto-Dig:MUR 7157 document-graph pass
summary: Random DNC-target pass expanded MUR 7157 from a seed matter-page reference into a source-backed regulatory-disposition record and a narrower document-level provenance recursion.

data.research_question: What does the primary FEC record establish about MUR 7157, and which document-level provenance gaps remain before the complaint, responses, evidence, counsel analysis, and final disposition form a complete claim graph?
data.method: User explicitly pinned selection to the DNC dataset. On current main 880b012ed436214e9ca29250d995ba1a5a1ed5cc, five queued public-source targets were read from the canonical DNC Project Veritas seed packet. Reproducible seed 1252985073849599857 was derived from SHA-256(main|2026-08-18T16:39-04:00|dnc-random-target); Python MT19937 choice selected starintel:investigation-target:fec-mur-7157-document-graph. Repository search confirmed the existing seed source starintel:source:fec-mur-7157 but no later canonical MUR 7157 expansion. Primary-source research then reviewed the FEC MUR 7157 matter page, the May 2, 2018 First General Counsel's Report, and the FEC weekly disposition summary. The report was analyzed at allegation-cluster and recommendation level. PDF screenshot retrieval was attempted as required but the FEC PDF screenshot backend returned cache-miss errors; parsed FEC PDF text remained available and was not supplemented with OCR guesses.
classification_rules: Respondent denials are not independently verified facts.
A no-reason-to-believe disposition is recorded as the Commission's enforcement finding, not as proof that every underlying factual assertion was false.
Documented payments do not by themselves establish prohibited coordination.
Keep complaint, response, OGC analysis, Commission disposition, and later civil-litigation evidence as separate evidentiary layers.

findings.finding: MUR 7157 alleged prohibited or excessive in-kind contributions and related reporting violations arising from alleged coordinated communications among the DNC/HFA and outside groups or consultants.
The First General Counsel's Report grouped the factual theories into Donald Ducks, paid protesters, the Wisconsin Fall Plan/GOTV proposal, and shared electoral strategy or messaging.

The record states the DNC reported $183,408.93 in 2016 payments to Mobilize; documentation identified $41,338.95 as related to Donald Ducks, while the remaining $142,069.98 was not itemized in the materials described by OGC.

OGC recommended, and the Commission approved, no-reason-to-believe findings because the record did not support the alleged prohibited or excessive coordinated contributions; the related reporting theory therefore also failed.
The existing corpus still lacks one stable canonical source record per MUR 7157 filing and explicit claim-to-response-to-finding edges.
